title: Precision curve mapping — Optimize walkthrough: INT8 vs FP8
summary: Redwood AE + SE demo the Optimize console's precision/latency visualization and sandbox. Focus on INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs for Aurora's conversational summarization model; discussed fidelity thresholds, rollback/fallback rules, telemetry to ship, and SOC2/KMS questions. Agreed to run a 2-week sandbox with side-by-side microbench and a short fidelity checklist.
transcript:
00:00 Sofia Ramirez: alright thanks everyone for joining, um this is Sofia from Redwood, i'll hand it over to Ethan for the demo in a minute.
00:18 Ethan Cole: hey team, yeah hey Maya, hi Priya, Liam, um today we want to show the Optimize console 'precision curve' view, and then run a quick sandbox compare between INT8 and FP8 profiles for your summarization workload. some of the names might look like, uh in the UI it's Optimize (sometimes the export says Optima) but same thing.
00:43 Dr. Maya Patel: great thanks, quick reminder we are running a 1.5B LLM forked model, fairly long context, average 1,200 tokens, 95% calls are request->summarize user session transcripts. latency budget is 350ms 95th, cost target is to cut per-token by ~40% vs current hosted.
01:05 Ethan Cole: perfect, that helps. i'll start with the curve — this shows measured fidelity (ROUGE-ish proxy + custom test set) on the y axis vs p99 latency on the x. blue is FP16 baseline, orange is FP8 profile, green is INT8 tuned profile.
01:30 Speaker 1: sorry could you repeat the axis labels?
01:33 Ethan Cole: sure — y is fidelity score (higher better), x is latency p99 in ms. you can pick different prompt types, we loaded your five seed prompts from the shared spreadsheet, in case the transcription changed some tokens, you'll see slight differences.
01:55 Liam O'Connor: the prompts in the sheet have a lot of edge cases — abbreviations, timestamps, so we worry about fidelity drop with INT8.
02:05 Ethan Cole: yeah totally — that's why the console surfaces per-prompt delta and the worst-case waterfall. for example, prompt 3 in your set shows INT8 drops the score from 0.81 to 0.68 on our metric, but FP8 is 0.79.
02:30 Priya Menon: so what's the cost delta on the same workload?
02:34 Ethan Cole: rough numbers from the microbench: FP16 baseline token cost X, FP8 around -28% unit cost, INT8 around -46%. latency wise, FP8 is usually 10-20% faster, INT8 can be faster but sometimes increases tail latency due to extra dequantization overhead in our runtime if the sequence lengths spike.
03:00 Sofia Ramirez: and important operational note — we support runtime fallbacks. you can set per-route fidelity thresholds that trigger fallback to FP8 or FP16 in the same deployment. that way you guard the worst-case prompts.
03:20 Dr. Maya Patel: that fallback sounds good. how does the console surface false positives — cases where a fallback would trigger unnecessarily?
03:26 Ethan Cole: console gives a sampling rate option — default 1% — and shows 'observed triggers' vs 'simulated triggers' so you can see estimated false positive rate. it's probabilistic but you can tune sampling up.
03:45 Speaker 2: (inaudible) what about KV cache behavior with INT8? we've had trouble with cache corruption with other stacks.
03:53 Ethan Cole: good question — we call it KV cache but in transcripts sometimes it's K V cash. the runtime keeps quantization metadata separately; in our tests we haven't seen corruption, but we do recommend a short warmup traffic profile during rollout to validate cache correctness.
04:15 Liam O'Connor: security wise — we need KMS & on-prem keys, also strong audit logs. can Redwood Private run this?
04:23 Sofia Ramirez: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM via the private control plane. audit logs and exportable tracing are included in our enterprise package. we'll share the SOC2 + ISO docs as part of the pack.
04:40 Dr. Maya Patel: are there any models where INT8 just fails?
04:44 Ethan Cole: rare but possible. models with very narrow activation ranges or heavy use of quant-sensitive ops can show big fidelity regressions. console flags those during model onboarding — we ran an automated sweep and flag high sensitivity layers.
05:05 Priya Menon: walk me through the sandbox plan — what data do you need from us?
05:12 Sofia Ramirez: ideally your representative prompt set (you've shared a good one), sample traffic distribution, and a short eval rubric — e.g., top 3 fidelity metrics you care about. we'll run parallel microbench on Dedicated sandbox cluster and give you the curve + per-prompt breakdown.
05:32 Ethan Cole: and we'll run the stress bench for 48 hours to observe tail behavior; we'll also capture telemetry for a rollback decision path — say thresholds for 95th latency, fidelity drop, error rate.
05:50 Dr. Maya Patel: what about differences between hosted vs dedicated? we prefer dedicated for predictability.
05:56 Ethan Cole: dedicated gives stable throughput and consistent p99; hosted can be cheaper at low volume but has multi-tenant variability. for your SLOs, Dedicated is the recommended path, and you can reserve burst capacity.
06:15 Liam O'Connor: any special config for batching? our average payload is long which complicates batching heuristics.
06:22 Ethan Cole: right — Optimize suggests batching window adjustments per-profile. INT8 tends to batch more efficiently because lower compute per token, but if you have a lot of long requests you might hit memory-bound situations; console will flag those with memory utilization heatmaps.
06:40 Sofia Ramirez: quick demo now — i'll share my screen, opening the precision curve for Aurora Labs sandbox.
06:48 [screen share starts]
07:10 Ethan Cole: here's the per-prompt waterfall, see prompt 7 has a big drop with INT8, the console adds a 'safe fallback' rule to push that prompt to FP8 only. you can apply rule by label or by regex.
07:32 Dr. Maya Patel: can we annotate prompts as 'sensitive' so they always avoid INT8?
07:36 Ethan Cole: yes, you can tag prompt groups and attach profile policies per-tag.
07:45 Speaker 1: (crosstalk) and can we see examples of decoded outputs side-by-side?
07:49 Ethan Cole: yep there's a 'compare' view — FP16 / FP8 / INT8 outputs with diff highlights and confidence deltas. note diffs aren't perfect — ROUGE proxy is a heuristic.
08:10 Priya Menon: show us a worst-case example.
08:15 Ethan Cole: here's prompt 3 — INT8 produced a truncated fact about dates, FP8 preserved them. console shows the token-level divergence and links back to your eval rubric.
08:35 Dr. Maya Patel: hmm that could be bad for regulatory summaries. how often did that happen in your run?
08:40 Ethan Cole: on the seed set it was 2% of cases for INT8, 0.6% for FP8. but that's why we test on your real traffic.
08:55 Sofia Ramirez: proposal — run a 2-week sandbox with: 1) microbench (throughput/latency/cost) 2) fidelity run on 10k sampled user transcripts 3) live canary at 5% with waterfall fallback rules.
09:15 Liam O'Connor: what resources needed on our side for the canary?
09:20 Ethan Cole: just a route tag in your router, we'll provide the rollout policy to apply via API or Console. Redwood SEs will assist the first canary.
09:32 Priya Menon: what's the instrumentation we get? token-level cost, p95/p99, per-prompt fidelity, and alerting?
09:38 Sofia Ramirez: yes all of that. plus anl (analytics) export to S3 and tracing to your datadog or jaeger collector.
09:50 Dr. Maya Patel: okay let's talk timelines — we want this in production by end of Q1. is 2-week sandbox realistic?
09:58 Ethan Cole: yes assuming we get your prompt set and sample traffic this week. onboarding and model sweep takes 3 business days, benching 10 days, then a canary for 3-5 days.
10:12 Speaker 2: quick nit — do you support mixed precision on a per-layer basis?
10:17 Ethan Cole: yes, our Optimize profiles can pin layer ranges to FP8 and INT8 where needed; console suggests candidate layer pins from the sensitivity sweep.
10:30 Liam O'Connor: any rules for rollback? we want a deterministic rollback path when fidelity drops.
10:36 Sofia Ramirez: you can set hard rollback triggers: e.g., if fidelity delta > 0.1 on key metrics OR p99 latency > 1.5x baseline, auto-rollback to previous profile. this is in the policy engine.
10:55 Dr. Maya Patel: are there known issues with hallucination increase under INT8?
11:00 Ethan Cole: sometimes you see more hallucinations if the quantization affects attention weights; however our eval includes hallucination detectors and shows per-class hallucination delta. FP8 usually balances hallucination risk and cost best.
11:22 Priya Menon: ok, security: we need logs for audit in a PII-safe way. can you redact before export?
11:29 Sofia Ramirez: yes console can redact matches or export only hashed tokens; we'll work with your compliance team on the exact schema.
11:40 Ethan Cole: also quick note: for on-prem/private, the runtime kernel selection is adjusted for your GPU architecture — intel GPUs need different kernels; we'll surface that in the onboarding report.
11:58 Dr. Maya Patel: can we bring our own quantization knobs? e.g., asymmetric vs symmetric, per-channel clipping.
12:05 Ethan Cole: yes you can customize the qprofile; Optimize provides recommended defaults plus advanced knobs for per-channel quant and clipping thresholds. advanced mode requires SE assistance.
12:22 Sophia (sic): (laughs) my name spelled Sophia in the chat sometimes, but it's Sofia.
12:28 Priya Menon: (laughs) noted.
12:35 Ethan Cole: nearing the end, quick risk list: INT8 can reduce cost most but increases testing complexity; FP8 is a good middle ground; maintain a short warmup, per-prompt exemptions, and rollback rules.
12:55 Dr. Maya Patel: agreed. last question: are there competitors who do this better? we've seen claims from Vertex and some smaller inference runtimes.
13:05 Sofia Ramirez: competitors like Vertex AI and some vendor runtimes support quant but they often lack the integrated per-prompt fidelity tooling and rollout policies. some open-source stacks like TorchServe need more orchestration to match our fallback semantics. we'll include a competitor comparison doc.
13:25 Liam O'Connor: ok for next steps let's capture action items.
13:30 [meeting recap and action items readout]
13:40 Sofia Ramirez: recap — we'll send the sandbox proposal and SOC2/KMS docs, SE will run an onboarding sweep, and we'll schedule the kick-off.
13:55 Dr. Maya Patel: thanks all, that's great.
14:00 [call ends]

Sofia Ramirez: send sandbox proposal, pricing ranges, SOC2 & ISO docs, KMS integration notes (due: 2026-11-06)
Dr. Maya Patel: provide 10k sampled transcripts + eval rubric (due: 2026-11-05)
Liam O'Connor: provision test route for 5% canary and share access (due: 2026-11-08)
